title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

sampleTestCases.description: Basic case with answer at the beginning
Answer in the middle of the array
Duplicate values that sum to target

hiddenTestCases.description: Answer at the end of the array

progressiveHints: Think about what value you need to find for each element to reach the target.
For each number, the complement is target - number. How can you quickly check if you've seen the complement before?
A hash map (JavaScript Map or object) can store values you've already visited, allowing O(1) lookups for the complement.
hints.keyInsight: Use a hash map to store each number's index as you iterate, then check if the complement (target - current number) already exists in the map.

edgeCases: Large numbers near the constraint boundary
Answer indices at the end of the array

alternativeApproaches.name: Brute Force
alternativeApproaches.description: Use two nested loops to check every pair of numbers. For each element, iterate through the rest of the array to find a complement that sums to the target.

alternativeApproaches.name: Hash Map (Optimal)
alternativeApproaches.description: Iterate through the array once, storing each number and its index in a hash map. For each element, check if the complement (target - current) already exists in the map.

alternativeApproaches.name: Sorting with Two Pointers
alternativeApproaches.description: Sort a copy of the array with original indices, then use two pointers from both ends to find the pair. Note: requires tracking original indices.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if:
1. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets.
2. Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
3. Every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.

examples.explanation: The single pair of parentheses is properly opened and closed.
All three types of brackets are properly opened and closed.
The opening parenthesis is closed by a square bracket, which is a mismatch.

hiddenTestCases.description: Single opening bracket with no closing
Interleaved brackets that are not properly nested

progressiveHints: Think about what data structure lets you match the most recent opening bracket with the current closing bracket.
A stack follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order. Push opening brackets onto the stack and pop when you encounter a closing bracket.
Use a hash map to pair each closing bracket with its matching opening bracket. When you see a closing bracket, check if the top of the stack matches.
hints.keyInsight: Use a stack to track opening brackets. When you encounter a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be the matching opening bracket. If the stack is empty at the end, the string is valid.

edgeCases: Interleaved but not properly nested brackets like ([)]

alternativeApproaches.name: Stack with Hash Map
alternativeApproaches.description: Use a stack to track opening brackets. For each closing bracket, check if the top of the stack is the matching opening bracket using a hash map for bracket pairs. If the stack is empty at the end, the string is valid.

alternativeApproaches.name: Replace Pairs Iteratively
alternativeApproaches.description: Repeatedly replace all adjacent matching pairs '()', '[]', '{}' with empty strings until no more replacements can be made. If the resulting string is empty, the input was valid.

title: Container With Most Water
description:
You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of the ith line are (i, 0) and (i, height[i]).

Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container, such that the container contains the most water.

Return the maximum amount of water a container can store.

Notice that you may not slant the container.

examples.explanation: The vertical lines at index 1 (height 8) and index 8 (height 7) form a container with area min(8,7) * (8-1) = 49.
The only container possible has area min(1,1) * (1-0) = 1.

sampleTestCases.description: Classic example with optimal pair in the middle
Minimum length array with equal heights
Optimal pair at the two ends of the array

hiddenTestCases.description: Small array where inner pair is optimal
Tall line in the middle with shorter lines around it
Maximum height values with minimum length
All zero heights produce zero area

progressiveHints: The area between two lines is determined by the shorter line and the distance between them. How can you maximize both factors?
Start with the widest possible container (first and last lines). Which pointer should you move inward to potentially find a larger area?
Always move the pointer pointing to the shorter line inward. Moving the taller line can never increase the area since the width decreases and the height is limited by the shorter line.
hints.keyInsight: Use two pointers starting at both ends. The area is limited by the shorter line, so always move the shorter pointer inward to potentially find a taller line that increases the area.

edgeCases: Maximum height values at the constraint boundary
Optimal pair at the ends of the array

alternativeApproaches.name: Brute Force
alternativeApproaches.description: Check every pair of lines and calculate the area for each pair. Track the maximum area found. For each pair (i, j), the area is min(height[i], height[j]) * (j - i).

alternativeApproaches.name: Two Pointers (Optimal)
alternativeApproaches.description: Use two pointers starting at the leftmost and rightmost lines. Calculate the area, then move the pointer pointing to the shorter line inward. The key insight is that moving the shorter pointer is the only way to potentially find a larger area, since the width is decreasing.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

A substring is a contiguous non-empty sequence of characters within a string.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.
The answer is "wke", with the length of 3. Notice that "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.

constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

sampleTestCases.description: Repeating pattern with longest unique substring at the start
Longest unique substring in the middle

hiddenTestCases.description: All unique characters — entire string is the answer
Tricky case where the window must skip past a repeated character
Duplicate at the start with unique character at the end

progressiveHints: Think about how you can examine substrings efficiently without checking every possible one.
A sliding window lets you expand and shrink a range of characters. What data structure helps you quickly check if a character is already in the current window?
Use a Set (or Map) to track characters in the current window. When you encounter a duplicate, shrink the window from the left until the duplicate is removed.
hints.keyInsight: Use a sliding window with two pointers and a Set to track characters in the current window. Expand the right pointer to include new characters, and shrink from the left when a duplicate is found.

edgeCases: All unique characters (entire string is the answer)
String with spaces and special characters
Duplicate that requires the window to jump forward

alternativeApproaches.name: Brute Force
alternativeApproaches.description: Check every possible substring and verify if it contains all unique characters. Track the maximum length found. For each starting index, expand the substring until a duplicate is found or the string ends.

alternativeApproaches.name: Sliding Window with Set
alternativeApproaches.description: Use two pointers to maintain a window of unique characters. Expand the right pointer to add characters. When a duplicate is found, shrink from the left by removing characters until the duplicate is gone. Track the maximum window size.

codeSolutions.python:
def length_of_longest_substring(s):
    char_set = set()
    left = 0
    max_len = 0
    for right in range(len(s)):
        while s[right] in char_set:
            char_set.remove(s[left])
            left += 1
        char_set.add(s[right])
        max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)
    return max_len

alternativeApproaches.name: Sliding Window with Map (Optimized)
alternativeApproaches.description: Use a Map to store each character's most recent index. When a duplicate is found, jump the left pointer directly past the previous occurrence instead of shrinking one character at a time. This avoids redundant iterations.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

examples.explanation: Since intervals [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, merge them into [1,6].

sampleTestCases.description: Second interval starts before the first

hiddenTestCases.description: One large interval absorbs all others
Large interval at the end absorbs all after sorting

progressiveHints: What happens if you sort the intervals by their start time? How does that simplify finding overlaps?
After sorting, overlapping intervals will be adjacent. Compare each interval's start with the previous interval's end to decide whether to merge.
Maintain a result array. For each interval, either merge it with the last interval in the result (if overlapping) or append it as a new interval.
hints.keyInsight: Sort intervals by start time, then iterate through them. If the current interval overlaps with the last merged interval (current start <= last end), extend the last interval's end. Otherwise, add the current interval to the result.

edgeCases: Intervals not given in sorted order
Intervals that share a single endpoint

alternativeApproaches.name: Sort and Merge (Optimal)
alternativeApproaches.description: Sort intervals by start time. Iterate through the sorted intervals, maintaining a merged result array. For each interval, if it overlaps with the last interval in the result (its start is less than or equal to the last interval's end), merge them by extending the end. Otherwise, add it as a new interval.

alternativeApproaches.name: Connected Components
alternativeApproaches.description: Build a graph where each interval is a node and edges connect overlapping intervals. Find connected components using BFS or DFS. Each component merges into one interval by taking the minimum start and maximum end. This approach is less efficient but conceptually demonstrates the overlap relationship.
